answer: Behavioral Echo Clustering. Each identity's action log is scanned for repeated decision sequences that echo across supposedly unrelated accounts; clusters above a similarity threshold flag a shared operator. A fable of independent agents thus collapses into one. Enforcement freezes cluster payouts and requires fresh, independently seeded registration, so every extra identity costs the attacker a full behavioral profile plus forfeited earnings — a mesa of duplicated effort they must rebuild from zero each time.
